jobs.title: Enterprise/Solution Architect – Infrastructure & Cloud
jobs.location:
Position Summary/ Department Summary:
The Enterprise/Solution Architect – Infrastructure & Cloud defines, designs, governs, and advances the organization's enterprise infrastructure and cloud architecture. The role provides strategic and technical leadership across AWS, Microsoft Azure, hybrid cloud, data centers, networking, telecommunications, compute, storage, virtualization, and supporting enterprise technologies.

Key Responsibilities:
Enterprise Architecture & Strategy
  • Develop infrastructure and cloud architecture principles, standards, reference architectures, and technology roadmaps.
  • Define current-state, target-state, and transition architectures. Identify gaps, dependencies, and technical debt.
  • Take part in architecture governance and technology investment decisions, using TOGAF-aligned practices.
Cloud Architecture & Modernization
  • Design secure, resilient, scalable, and cost-effective solutions across AWS, Azure, GCP, and hybrid/on-premises environments.
  • Define landing zones, connectivity, identity integration, security controls, and workload placement.
  • Guide cloud migration, modernization, and automation. Support CCoE guardrails and FinOps practices.
Infrastructure & Network Architecture
  • Architect WAN/LAN, SD-WAN, telecommunications, data center, compute, storage, and virtualization environments.
  • Set standards for availability, performance, resiliency, and disaster recovery.
  • Evaluate products and designs for security, lifecycle risk, and total cost of ownership.
Solution Design & Governance
  • Lead architecture assessments and solution designs for complex infrastructure and cloud initiatives.
  • Produce diagrams, design documents, decision records, and implementation roadmaps.
  • Review vendor proposals against enterprise standards. Provide guidance from planning through operational handoff.
Innovation & Cost Optimization
  • Evaluate infrastructure as code, automation, AI-enabling infrastructure, and emerging platforms.
  • Recommend consolidation, cost optimization, and technical debt reduction.
Intake, Delivery & Capacity Planning
  • Support a lean technology intake process that assesses architectural impact and prioritizes demand.
  • Use CMDB data to understand assets, dependencies, and change impacts, and promote data quality.
  • Manage architecture backlogs and decisions in Jira, using sound project management practices.
  • Partner with leaders and the PMO on capacity planning, forecasting, and sequencing of work.
Collaboration & Leadership
  • Act as a trusted advisor to IT leadership, project teams, and business stakeholders.
  • Work with Cloud, Network, Telecom, Data Center, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise Architecture teams.
  • Explain technical tradeoffs to both technical and nontechnical audiences and mentor technical staff.

Minimum Qualifications
Education:
  • Bachelor's Degree or 10 years of experience as an Enterprise/Solution Architect required.
  • Preferred area of study: Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.

Experience:
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in enterprise IT infrastructure, cloud, or related technical disciplines
  • 5+ years in enterprise, solution, infrastructure, or cloud architecture roles
  • Demonstrated experience designing complex enterprise infrastructure and AWS or Azure or GCP hybrid-cloud solutions
  • Experience developing architecture standards, reference architectures, and roadmaps
  • Experience in large, complex, highly available or regulated organizations; healthcare, academic medical center, or research preferred
  • Experience using CMDB platforms (such as ServiceNow CMDB) to analyze configuration items, service dependencies, and infrastructure changes
  • Experience with Jira and participation in lean intake, demand management, or project delivery processes

Licensure/ Certifications:
  • TOGAF certification required
  • Azure Solutions Architect Expert; relevant infrastructure, networking, or cybersecurity certifications preferred

jobs.title: Healthcare Data Analyst I
jobs.location:
Position/ Department Summary
The Musculoskeletal Digital Innovation and Informatics Program (MDI2) at the Department of Orthopedics and Sports Medicine at Boston Children's Hospital and Harvard Medical School seeks a Healthcare Data Analyst I to serve as the dedicated data analytics and data management resource supporting the Sports Medicine Research and Translational Innovation (SPORTI) program. 

This position will support a growing portfolio of prospective, longitudinal, registry-based, and multicenter research studies. Working closely with investigators, research staff, and biostatisticians, the analyst will leverage MDI2 infrastructure to develop, maintain, and optimize research databases, reporting tools, and data workflows. The role will support data quality, reporting, standardization, analysis-ready datasets, and multicenter studies where SPORTI serves as a Data Coordinating Center (DCC), while helping build scalable research data infrastructure across the SPORTI portfolio. 

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Design, develop, maintain, and optimize research databases, reporting systems, dashboards, and analytical tools supporting SPORTI research programs. 
  • Collaborate with investigators, coordinators, statisticians, and administrative staff to ensure data systems and reports are accurate, interpretable, and aligned with study objectives. 
  • Develop and maintain REDCap projects, data dictionaries, validation rules, database specifications, and related documentation to support standardized data management practices. 
  • Perform data validation, quality assurance, discrepancy resolution, and data cleaning activities to ensure data integrity and analysis readiness. 
  • Create and maintain reports, dashboards, visualizations, and study metrics related to enrollment, follow-up completion, data quality, site performance, and research outcomes. 
  • Prepare, validate, and document datasets for statistical analysis, abstracts, manuscripts, grant applications, and presentations. 
  • Support multicenter studies and registries by coordinating database activities, site onboarding, data harmonization, quality monitoring, discrepancy resolution, and reporting, including studies where SPORTI serves as the Data Coordinating Center. 
  • Maintain large research databases and repositories, supporting database standards, key data elements, workflow documentation, and operational continuity across projects and staff transitions. 
  • Develop standardized workflows, SOPs, training materials, and best practices that improve consistency, efficiency, and data quality across SPORTI programs.  

 
Minimum Qualifications 
Education: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field is required. Master’s degree is preferred. ​​​​​​​
Experience: 
  • Expertise in Python programming is required. 
  • Expertise in SQL and database querying is required. 
  • Experience in the use of large language models and their applications is required. 
  • Experience developing dashboards, visualizations, and automated reporting solutions is required. 
  • Experience building scalable data processing pipelines for large healthcare datasets is preferred. 
  • Familiarity with NLP or clinical text analysis is preferred. 
  • Experience supporting multicenter studies or coordinating-center activities is preferred.

jobs.title: Computational Health Informatics Data Manager II
jobs.location:
Position Summary
The Labs of Cognitive Neuroscience at Boston Children’s Hospital seeks a full-time Computational Health Informatics Data Manager II to support research on development, neurodevelopmental disorders, and rare genetic conditions, including:
  • Baby Steps Project: A longitudinal study tracking EEG and cognitive, language, and social development from infancy through early childhood to improve early identification of developmental delays and autism in diverse populations.
  • Data infrastructure initiatives, including database development and administration and harmonization of neuroimaging, behavioral, and clinical data across longitudinal studies for secondary analysis.
This hybrid position is based at Two Brookline Place, Brookline, MA, with a minimum two-year commitment and potential for continued employment and professional growth based on performance, project needs, and funding.

The role oversees data quality across assessments, including questionnaires, behavioral observations, neuroimaging, and medical records, from collection through publication. Regular participant interaction is not required, though understanding data collection procedures is helpful, and opportunities to shadow study visits are available.

Key Responsibilities
  • Oversee quality and management of longitudinal, multimodal research data. Develop audit tools and workflows to reduce errors; document changes to study measures and collection procedures, including version control.
  • Develop and maintain data infrastructure, including REDCap projects and Python tools. Collaborate with PIs and research staff to design, build, and validate a SQL database for large, harmonized datasets; ensure final data outputs are complete and accurate.
  • Improve data processing and harmonization pipelines throughout the study lifecycle. Support questionnaire, clinical, EEG, and medical record data using established standards and software.
  • Develop scoring scripts and automated workflows for data cleaning, preprocessing, and statistical analysis. Use AI-assisted tools where appropriate and validate outputs.
  • Coordinate data access and sharing, including collaborator requests, data use agreements, secure transfers, repository submissions (e.g., NDA), and IRB-required changes.
  • Train data collection staff on data management workflows and technologies; guide staff developing data tools.
  • Support progress reports and grant submissions by preparing preliminary datasets and streamlining recurring reports.
Minimum Qualifications
Education:
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, biomedical engineering, biostatistics, biomedical data science, or a related field.
Experience:
  • Minimum 2 years of full-time clinical research data analysis or coordination experience, or equivalent.
  • Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and experience with REDCap.
  • Experience cleaning and validating large datasets, maintaining documentation, and preparing data for statistical analysis using scalable workflows.
  • Experience with longitudinal datasets and harmonizing complex health research data across studies; knowledge of developmental science and neuroscience.
  • Strong communication and writing skills, including collaboration with multiple investigators and training research staff.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to data accuracy and completeness; ability to work independently and solve problems proactively.
  • Familiarity with clinical research data protection best practices, including HIPAA requirements.
  • SQL programming and relational database design experience, including databases for large research datasets, preferred.
  • Experience with Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) preferred.
  • Experience processing and managing EEG data preferred.

jobs.title: Research Software Developer II
jobs.location:
Position Summary
Seeking an experienced software developer with experience in medical imaging and computer graphics and strong proficiency in Python coding. The role requires problem-solving skills that include strong background in 3D geometry, linear algebra, and numerical analysis. The ideal candidate will have experience in graphics APIs or toolkits including VTK and in segmentation software such as the Slicer platform. This individual will help develop custom software applications for 3D modeling and computational planning for surgical repairs in patients with congenital heart disease. This will be a role that integrates with an existing software development team and builds upon existing elements within the Slicer platform and ecosystem. This role will require close interface with engineering and clinical teams who are developing and implementing computational planning within congenital cardiac repair.

Key Responsibilities 
  • Researches and identifies the requirements for new and/or enhanced software applications, functionality, web services, and other research information system needs.
  • Works collaboratively with multiple stakeholders in the iterative assessment, design, implementation, and improvement of enhanced research software capabilities and new efforts.
  • Drafts (or directs drafting of) detailed software architecture plans, application program interfaces (APIs), operational requirements in the form of documents, diagrams, mappings, RFPs, project schedules, technical summaries, status reports, and other project architecture and related management reports for evaluation and review.
  • Creates or participates in creation of software, network, API, and other relevant documentation for the design, development, iterative refinement, testing, and performance tracking of software development activities and related informatics systems processes.
  • Maintains current knowledge of state-of-the-art and best-practices software design and development.
  • Participates in evaluation of applications, supporting systems, and hardware environment as well as future technology trends in order to assist management with IT strategy and planning.
  • Disseminates this knowledge to management and staff to guide in research software development and operation.
  • Works with team members to manage the work of technical personnel as it relates to the operations, maintenance, and development of the software.
  • Monitors the tasks performed and provide guidance, mentoring, and management input on the execution of these tasks as they relate to the support of the software and software development process.
  • Maintains current knowledge of the software, supporting systems, and software development life-cycle as well as future technology trends in order to assist with research project strategy and planning.
  • Disseminates this knowledge to management, staff, and stakeholders in a technical leadership role.
  • Establishes and maintains relationships with senior leadership of the research investigator and developer communities to understand business requirements and goals.
  • Identifies and prioritizes software architecture and development to support research objectives.
  • Ensures or arranges for appropriate technical support for stakeholders based on project needs.

  • A bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering or a related field.

jobs.title: Bioinformatics Scientist
jobs.location:
Position Summary:
Research Informatics supports basic, translational, and clinical research by providing researchers with access to digital tools and technologies. Our computing environment consists of high-performance computing clusters, virtual machines, PetaByte-scale high-performance storage and cloud platforms. We work with scientists to develop solutions in support of cutting-edge research ranging from lattice light-sheet microscopy to CryoEM, genomics, and informatics.

You will work with PhD-level bioinformatics scientists and researchers who have single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data to investigate mouse and human diseases as well as with other pediatric scientists at BCH. The primary responsibilities will be building pipelines for the analysis, integration and sharing of these data. The ideal candidate should have enthusiasm for developing collaborative relationships and a desire to foster the use of bioinformatics data in research studies.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Providing computational support by applying a wide range of bioinformatics tools and technologies; With supervision and direction, completing assignments in the required timeframe while consistently adhering to standard operating procedures and best practices; adapting to a changing environment, resolving problems associated with assignments and seeking supervisor assistance when needed.
  • Routinely co-leading or participating in research computing projects with other members from the BCH research community; setting goals and objectives for projects and demonstrating achievement of those goals and objectives; coordinating work activities with other stakeholders; contributing to the resulting presentations and/or publications.
  • Training staff and researchers; effectively tailoring presentations.
  • Communicating scientific findings clearly through presentations, email, memos, and scientific publications; presenting progress at project and departmental meetings; facilitating productive discussions and problem-solving.

jobs.title: Medical Lab Scientist II - Day shift

Performs a variety of routine and highly specialized diagnostic tests and specialized procedures.  Assures quality of the results and communicates relevance of results to other health care professionals.

jobs.title: Operating Engineer

Position Summary:
In accordance with established methods and procedures, performs minor repairs and basic preventive maintenance of designated equipment and operating systems within the hospital. In response to service requests and emergency alarms, evaluates nature of services required and refers problems requiring skilled intervention to licensed trade personnel.

  • 2 years of occupationally – specific education.
  • Associates degree preferred
Experience:
  • 4 years of experience required.
Shift/hours:
  • Tuesday – Saturday:  3:00pm – 11:00pm
